title: filter - Filters - Tailwind CSS
content_text: FILTERS filter Utilities for applying filters to an element. Class Styles filter-none filter: none; filter-() filter: var(); filter-[] filter: ; EXAMPLES Basic example Use utilities like blur-xs and grayscale to apply filters to an element: blur-xs grayscale combined You can combine the following filter utilities: blur, brightness, contrast, drop-shadow, grayscale, hue-rotate, invert, saturate, and sepia. Removing filters Use the filter-none utility to remove all of the filters applied to an element: Using a custom value Use the filter-[] syntax to set the filter based on a completely custom value: For CSS variables, you can also use the filter-() syntax: This is just a shorthand for filter-[var()] that adds the var() function for you automatically. Applying on hover Prefix a filter utility with a variant like hover:* to only apply the utility in that state: Learn more about using variants in the variants documentation. Responsive design Prefix a filter utility with a breakpoint variant like md: to only apply the utility at medium screen sizes and above: Learn more about using variants in the variants documentation. mask-type blur
